memos.argument: A forged connecting rod is a part suitable solely or principally for diesel (heading 8408) engines. Note 2(b) to Section XVI sends such parts to 8409; the engine is for Class 8 trucks, so 8409.99.91 (parts to be installed in vehicles of heading 8704 etc.) applies and has a statistical line 8409.99.91.10 'Connecting rods'. Not a part of general use and not named in any other heading.
exclusions_against: Section XVI note 2(a): parts that fall within another heading of ch. 84/85 (other than 8409 etc.) go to that heading; 8483 competes if a connecting rod is deemed a crank/transmission part.
Section XVI note 1(g): parts of general use (section XV) excluded; not applicable to a dedicated connecting rod.
Ruling I83991 concerns a marine diesel elbow in 8409.99, only an analogy; no connecting-rod ruling found.

memos.argument: The item is a forged alloy steel product; 7228.40 covers other bars and rods of alloy steel 'not further worked than forged', and ruling N241159 classified a forged alloy steel bar there. If the rod is an unmachined rough forging blank not yet dedicated, a forged steel form could stay in ch. 72.
exclusions_against: 7228 covers bars, rods, angles, shapes and sections; a forged connecting rod with a shaped big-end and small-end is an identifiable engine part, not a bar or rod.
Section XV/ch. 72 is semi-finished steel; a part dedicated to engines goes to 8409 per Section XVI note 2.
Steel alloy type unknown; 7228 needs 'other alloy steel' per chapter 72 note 1(f).

memos.argument: 8483 covers transmission shafts, crankshafts and cranks and parts thereof. A connecting rod links piston to crank and converts reciprocating to rotary motion, so it can be argued to be a crank-type element or a part of cranks; Section XVI note 2(a) says parts in 8483 take that heading and not 8409. Rulings put crankshafts (G83876) in 8483.10 and engine plain bearings (N188079) in 8483.30 over 8409 via note 2(a). Best code under 8483.10 is 8483.10.50.00 other transmission shafts and cranks.
exclusions_against: 8483 names crankshafts, cranks, bearings, gears; connecting rods are not named, so they are not 'goods included in' 8483 and note 2(a) does not displace 8409.
Rulings found concern crankshafts and bearings, not connecting rods.
Heading 8409 has a specific 10-digit 'Connecting rods' line, which indicates the tariff itself treats them under 8409.
